page: UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is a compute-oriented virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 2 shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of system memory (2.0 GB per core), and a bundled 50 GB local SSD. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and operates without dedicated GPU acceleration. The underlying AMD processor features advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, AES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data demonstrates exceptionally high single-threaded performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests (3836.96) and Geekbench single-core execution (2322.0), along with top-tier throughput in single-threaded compression algorithms such as gzip (40.92 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (17.05 GB/sec). Text processing via Geekbench also registers in the upper quartile. However, overall multi-core capabilities and aggregate compute metrics reflect its modest two-core footprint, showing average to lower-tier results in multi-core stress-ng (7660.14) and Geekbench multi-core (4032.0).

Memory and complex multi-threaded workloads present distinct performance boundaries. Uncached read bandwidth is solid at 67.23 GB/sec, but cached small-block bandwidth and the overall PassMark memory score rank in the lower brackets. Highly parallel tasks like clang compilation, ray tracing, and Redis operations are restricted by the core allocation and memory capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency is strongest when leveraging the server's single-core burst capability for lightweight execution paths, rather than wide parallel processing.

UpCloud PREMIUM-2xCPU-4GB is well-suited for single-threaded utilities, static web serving (benchmarked at 8.78 GB/sec), small-scale edge services, and lightweight background automation. It can also manage modest AI inference tasks on lightweight models, reaching 681.26 prompt tokens per second on 135M parameter models.

Designed with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it includes hardware support for AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, with no dedicated GPU. Performance metrics reveal outstanding single-core execution, ranking in the top tier for Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression. Conversely, multi-threaded tasks, ray tracing, and memory-intensive operations are constrained by the physical core count and memory capacity. It provides efficient single-threaded throughput, making it suitable for static web serving, text parsing, light utility tasks, and microservice workloads.
